schemes.label: IASP (Informative Authoring Semantics Profile)
schemes.description: IASP: names for what a passage of long-form nonfiction is doing — its delivery role relative to the main flow (Axis A) and the rhetorical, expository or stance-signalling work it does (Axis B). Terms compose as delivery.modifier (e.g. note.insight, sidebar.example). Informative, not normative: nothing is required and untagged text is valid.

terms.label: analogy
terms.scopeNote: Comparative explanation.

terms.label: appendix
terms.scopeNote: Material outside the main narrative flow.

terms.label: argument and reasoning
terms.scopeNote: Modifiers naming a move in the argument.

terms.label: assumption
terms.scopeNote: Declared premise.

terms.label: back-matter
terms.scopeNote: Build extension. Material closing the work after the main narrative (bibliography, index, colophon, etc.); counterpart to front-matter.

terms.label: background
terms.scopeNote: Contextual grounding. Example composition: sidebar.background.

terms.label: breadcrumb
terms.scopeNote: Pointer back to where an idea was introduced or forward to where it continues. note.breadcrumb (named as a common pattern in IASP Core) renders with a directional chevron; add .badge for the BREADCRUMB label.

terms.label: bridge
terms.scopeNote: Transitional connective text. Also used as a note variant (note.bridge, lavender badge) to stitch concepts together inside a chapter or appendix. In builds a bridge maps to ARIA role complementary and accepts .pre-pagebreak / .post-pagebreak.

terms.label: callout
terms.scopeNote: Build extension. A short aside lifted out of the flow with a light border-left treatment.

terms.label: case-study
terms.scopeNote: Extended real-world instance.

terms.label: caution
terms.scopeNote: Advice against overreach.

terms.label: chapter
terms.scopeNote: Primary unit of argument.

terms.label: checklist
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.checklist, teal ☐ badge). Indicative checklists, verification criteria or structured evidence markers.

terms.label: claim
terms.scopeNote: Supporting assertion.

terms.label: closing
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.closing, muted ∎ badge). Closing-note and endcap reflections.

terms.label: context
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.context, warm slate ◉ badge). Contextual framing that sets the scene or establishes background.

terms.label: contrast
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.contrast, inline ⇆ glyph). A short compare/contrast clarification between frameworks.

terms.label: counterpoint
terms.scopeNote: Alternative or opposing view.

terms.label: definition
terms.scopeNote: Clarification of a term. Also usable alone as a block (::: definition, green glossary frame). Example composition: note.definition.

terms.label: delivery role
terms.scopeNote: How a passage relates to the surrounding narrative flow: its placement and relationship to the main text. The leftmost term in a composition (delivery.modifier). Unmarked text is assumed to be main flow; one delivery role per passage is usually enough.

terms.label: diagnostic
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.diagnostic, blue 🔍 badge). Pattern-recognition checklists and diagnostic callouts.

terms.label: disclosure
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.disclosure, violet ◊ badge). Transparency notes: assumptions, limits, or what is being disclosed.

terms.label: endnotes
terms.scopeNote: Deferred ancillary content. The build's 'footnotes' class maps to doc-endnotes.

terms.label: epigraph
terms.scopeNote: Build extension. A quotation set at the head of a part, chapter or section.

terms.label: epigraph-inline
terms.scopeNote: Build extension. An epigraph set within the running text rather than as a heading block.

terms.label: example
terms.scopeNote: Concrete illustration. Also usable alone as a block (::: example, blue accent frame). Example composition: sidebar.example.

terms.label: exposition and support
terms.scopeNote: Modifiers naming material that explains, illustrates or grounds the argument.

terms.label: footnote
terms.scopeNote: Localized ancillary content. Example composition: footnote.counterpoint.

terms.label: front-matter
terms.scopeNote: Material framing the work (preface, introduction, etc.).

terms.label: gloss
terms.scopeNote: Brief explanatory note.

terms.label: idea
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.idea, inline 💡 glyph). A suggestion or generative thought offered in passing.

terms.label: implication
terms.scopeNote: Consequence of an argument.

terms.label: insight
terms.scopeNote: Moment of realization or reframing. As a note variant (note.insight) it renders with an asterism row.

terms.label: integration
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.integration, teal ∞ badge). Guidance on integrating or synthesising across frameworks.

terms.label: interlude
terms.scopeNote: Intentional pause or tonal shift.

terms.label: limitation
terms.scopeNote: Known constraint.

terms.label: major insight
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.insight.major, badge strip). An insight given more weight than the asterism form.

terms.label: methodology
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.methodology, indigo ⊢ badge). Explains how the analysis is conducted.

terms.label: misuse
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.misuse, red ✕ badge). Flags common misreadings or warns against weaponizing a framework.

terms.label: modifier
terms.scopeNote: What kind of work a passage is doing and what stance it signals: rhetorical function, reader guidance or epistemic stance. Qualifies a delivery role in a composition (delivery.modifier); one or two modifiers are usually enough.

terms.label: navigation
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.navigation, teal ⇢ badge). Reader-navigation breadcrumbs and orientation guides. The docs also list note.orientation for the same purpose, but iasp-semantics.lua has no 'orientation' variant, so it currently renders as a plain note.

terms.label: note
terms.scopeNote: Ancillary content tied to a point, but not necessarily a formal footnote. The most-composed role: the build recognises a fixed set of note variants (see the 'Note variants' collection), each with its own box style, written note.<variant>.

terms.label: notice
terms.scopeNote: Important framing information.

terms.label: part
terms.scopeNote: Major thematic division.

terms.label: prelude
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.prelude). An opening note that prepares the reader for what follows.

terms.label: provocation
terms.scopeNote: Intentionally unsettling prompt.

terms.label: qualification
terms.scopeNote: Limitation or nuance.

terms.label: reader navigation
terms.scopeNote: Modifiers that orient the reader within the book: where they are, where they came from, where they are going. Not a heading in IASP Core; groups build-supported note variants.

terms.label: reader signals and stance
terms.scopeNote: Modifiers that alert the reader or declare the author's epistemic or moral stance.

terms.label: reflection
terms.scopeNote: Interpretive or contemplative pause. Example: bridge.reflection.

terms.label: reflexive
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.reflexive, slate ⟲ badge). Reflexive cautions: the author or reader turning the analysis on themselves.

terms.label: responsibility
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.responsibility, amber ⚖ badge). Responsibility or accountability framing.

terms.label: scope
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.scope, warm copper ◎ badge). Delimits boundaries, applicability or evidentiary thresholds.

terms.label: section
terms.scopeNote: Subdivision within a chapter.

terms.label: series
terms.scopeNote: Optional super-division above parts; use only if helpful. Naming is configurable (see Part Naming).

terms.label: sidebar
terms.scopeNote: Optional digression or parallel track. Common compositions: sidebar.example, sidebar.background. Builds map it to epub:type aside and ARIA role complementary; .sidebar-block gives the full-width badge form.

terms.label: sidebar-inline
terms.scopeNote: Build extension. A sidebar that sits inside the prose, with a glyph on its first line rather than a badge header.

terms.label: synthesis
terms.scopeNote: Integration of ideas. As a note variant (note.synthesis, green ⊕ badge): a block that integrates multiple strands into a single takeaway.

terms.label: thesis
terms.scopeNote: Central claim. Example: section.thesis, to mark a major move.

terms.label: transition
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.transition, inline ⇥ glyph). Hand-off moments, scene shifts or narrative pivots.

terms.label: uncertainty
terms.scopeNote: Epistemic humility.

terms.label: usage
terms.scopeNote: Build extension (note.usage, steel-blue ⚙ badge). Guidance on how to apply a framework or idea.

terms.label: warning
terms.scopeNote: Risk, harm or moral alert. As a note variant (note.warning) it renders with a warning badge.

sets.label: Delivery roles in reading order
sets.description: IASP Core delivery roles in the order Semantic Vocabulary §6 lists them: framing, structural divisions from largest to smallest, connective and parallel text, then ancillary material.

sets.label: IASP Core
sets.description: The terms defined in IASP Core (Semantic Vocabulary §6–7): twelve delivery roles and twenty-one modifiers. Everything else in the scheme is a build extension or a grouping concept.

sets.label: Note variants
sets.description: Modifiers the build recognises after note (note.<variant>), each with its own box environment and badge or glyph: the keys of NOTE_VARIANT_CONFIG in iasp_tooling/lua/iasp-semantics.lua. Other modifiers composed with note still render, as a plain note box.
